Answer: B
Reason: The chest X-ray demonstrates enlargement of the central pulmonary arteries, specifically a prominent right descending pulmonary artery (pruned tree appearance), which is a classic radiographic sign of pulmonary hypertension secondary to chronic pulmonary embolism. The cardiac silhouette appears relatively normal in size, making severe right heart failure less likely than mild-to-moderate pulmonary vascular changes.
